s8d3855332931df: The MIG and HAMi-core models differ as follows:
s7bab9ee7bd1cad: Filtering and scoring directly from GPU Resources on Node, selecting the appropriate Node, GPU in HAMi-core mode
s997931513fdd72: Under MIG mode, the most appropriate template or instance is found based on the MIG example or the MIG template and matched by GPU memory
seb00798c57845b: Qos is achieved using libvgpu.so in the HAMi-core mode, so it is necessary to mount libvgpu.so and specify environmental variables according to the application resource, and eventually mount GPU to Pod
s52dd232ac1240e: MIG mode is the case of cutting MIG, and then mount the MIG instance to Pod
s63f49271ace8ce: The MIG model has the following advantages compared to the hami-core model:
s3e659786db6877: MIG splits GPU by hardware, making each virtual GPU run like a single physical GPU. Each virtual GPU has its own memory and computing resources and does not compete with other virtual GPUs to provide greater solitude.
sd9a682ec1e157f: : no need to use libvgpu.so to intercept CUDA API, which will improve performance
s99c87ea5d1be51: MIG avoids the failure of a task that affects the operation of other tasks, because each virtual GPU is independent. When a virtual GPU is in trouble, the computing resources and state of other virtual GPUs are not affected, thus improving system stability.
s969b2e1cea0118: Of course, the hami-core model has its own advantages:
s6dfe61fdc91654: You can slice any particle size core, memory.
s36796028dd8316: Both can be used in combination, depending on the context of their use.
